title: Amphibious stem-insect sheds light on colonization of land.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC lists no open-access full text, no PMCID, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links and no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI. One web search found only the Nature page, PubMed and press releases; no data deposit link.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract and a press summary: the paper describes one fossil specimen (Chosha praecursor, about 324 million years old) plus revisions of three other fossils, and runs a phylogenetic (family-tree) analysis on a morphological character matrix reported as 58 characters scored across 23 groups. I did not see the matrix itself.

a1_downloadable.note: No data deposit found: no PMCID, no supplement retrievable through Europe PMC, and no Zenodo/Dryad record on the DOI. The paper's own supplement on nature.com may hold the matrix, but it is behind the publisher site, which we don't scrape.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only data is a morphological character matrix (anatomical traits scored as states per taxon) and fossil images; there is no measured outcome column to predict. Any label (e.g. tree placement) would come out of the authors' phylogenetic inference.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be photographs of a handful of fossils or a small trait matrix; not seen in any file.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable: categorical anatomical character states, not measurements; not verified in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Press summary reports 58 characters across 23 taxa, i.e. about 23 rows, far below the 400-row minimum. Not verified in files, but even a tenfold error would still fail.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: under 1 MB (a small trait matrix), if it were available

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No files opened, so counts could not be checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any candidate label (whether a fossil is a stem-insect) is the output of the authors' own tree-building analysis computed from the same trait matrix, so it is circular.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible: the paper is a description of one fossil species and a 23-taxon family-tree analysis.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use scored anatomical traits of fossil and living arthropods to predict whether a fossil belongs to the insect lineage.
plain_idea.train_on: Anatomical trait scores per taxon; reported as about 23 taxa by 58 traits, not verified.
plain_idea.predict: Group membership (insect lineage or not), which here comes from the authors' own family-tree inference, not an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little: with ~23 examples, classical phylogenetic methods are the right tool and ML would add nothing a palaeontologist would use.

ml_idea: None viable: a single-fossil description with a ~23-taxon trait matrix offers no labelled dataset of ML scale.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; the project fails on data size and availability before compute matters.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the taxa in the character matrix: about 23 reported, which already kills it.

verdict_reason: Paleontology paper describing one fossil; the only data is a reported ~23-taxon by 58-trait matrix with no deposit found (A1), no measured label (A2), far too few rows (A5), and any label would be the authors' own tree inference (A8).
